theory.text: Match each paragraph with the heading that best summarises its main idea. A heading should describe the whole paragraph rather than one supporting detail. There are usually extra headings.
Key skills: Skimming and separating main ideas from examples.

guide.text: Read the heading list  skim each paragraph  write its main idea in a short phrase  match by overall meaning  eliminate headings that match only isolated details.

small.text: Paragraph: “Solar panels became cheaper to manufacture in the last decade. As prices fell, more households installed them, although output still depends on sunlight.”
Choose the best heading: A. How falling solar-panel costs encouraged adoption; B. Night-time electricity storage; C. The first solar inventor.

full.text: A. Early city parks were often designed primarily as formal landscapes. Their carefully arranged paths and lawns offered attractive scenery.B. More recently, park designers have begun including wetlands and wildflower areas to support insects and birds. These spaces provide habitat.C. Researchers are now exploring how residents participate in park planning. Community workshops reveal needs that designers might otherwise overlook.
Match paragraphs A–C to headings i–iv.i. Including residents in decisionsii. Parks designed mainly for appearanceiii. Designing parks to support wildlifeiv. How to build a playground

rows: Falling cost is linked to more home installations.
Wildlife habitat in wetland and wildflower areas.
Choosing FALSE when evidence is missing
Use FALSE only if the passage contradicts the statement; otherwise consider NOT GIVEN.
Choosing a heading because one word matches
Summarise the paragraph’s full main idea.
Answer using the evidence in the passage only.
Recheck NO MORE THAN ... WORDS instructions and spelling.
Check the complete sentence against evidence.
Spending too long on one question
Move on and return after easier questions.
Confusing a quoted opinion with the writer’s stance
Identify who holds the opinion before answering YES / NO / NOT GIVEN.
Filling a gap with an unsuitable word form
